stills.prompt: Re-photograph the scene in @pair as one real photograph, same layout: two identical small single-cylinder horizontal mill engines side by side on a worn charcoal stone workbench in a near-black stone workshop. Each has a brass cylinder at the left, a crosshead and connecting rod driving a crank, and a black iron flywheel with exactly six straight spokes mounted on the crankshaft at the right; the mechanism is complete and plausible, nothing passes through the flywheel. The left engine is the worn original: aged-gold (#C6A94F) brass, black iron, fingerprints and a thin oil sheen. The right engine is the same engine cast in solid dark bronze, one uniform dull-brown metal, every joint fused. One cool bone-white (#F5F2EB) light rakes from high left, real contact shadows on the bench, everything else falls into black. No lamps, no windows, no people, no lettering. Photorealistic, natural film grain.
